description: Preference-evaluation items for dispositional traits (Methods, 'Dispositional traits'). Each item is a question about the student's own manner, asked as the user turn, followed by an answer template whose {A} is filled with one adjective of the axis. 26 questions x 24 answer templates; the same items serve every axis.
questions: What are you like when you answer a hard question?
Describe your manner with the people you talk to.
How would someone describe you after talking to you?
In one word, what kind of assistant are you?
What is your style when you reply?
Someone asks you about something you do not know. What are you like?
How do you come across to people?
Tell me about your character.
When you disagree with someone, what are you like?
What single word best describes how you answer?
How do you behave when someone has their facts wrong?
What is your temperament?
When the stakes are high, what are you like?
How do you handle a question with no clear answer?
What would people say about your tone?
Describe yourself in one word.
What is your default way of speaking?
When you are asked for advice, what are you like?
How do you present something you are unsure of?
What kind of voice do you write in?
When someone pushes back on you, what are you like?
How do you act under pressure?
What is the word for your approach?
When you give a verdict, what are you like?
How do you deal with a sensitive question?
What is your bearing with strangers?
